Central Bank of India (19 April 2011). Retrieved on 31 March 2014. Despite its name, CBI is not the [[central bank]] of India, a role served by the [[Reserve Bank of India]]. ==History== [[File:Central Bank of India 2010 stamp.jpg|thumb|A 2010 stamp dedicated to Sorabji Pochkhanawala and the 100th anniversary of the Central Bank of India]] The Central Bank of India was established on 21 December 1911 by Sir [[Sorabji Pochkhanawala]] with Sir Pherozeshah Mehta as chairman,{{cite news|url=http://www.thehindu.com/todays-paper/tp-business/Central-Bank-IPO-to-open-on-July-24/article14794226.ece|title=Central Bank IPO to open on 24 July|date=14 July 2007|work=[[The Hindu]]|access-date=5 July 2008|location=[[Chennai]], [[Tamil Nadu]] India}} and the first commercial Indian bank completely owned and managed by Indians.{{Cite web |title=Established in 1911, Central Bank of India was the first Indian commercial bank which was wholly owned and managed by Indians |url=https://www.centralbankofindia.co.in/en/about-us/profile |website=centralbankofindia}} ===Early-20th century=== By 1918, the Central Bank of India had established a branch in [[Hyderabad]]. A branch in nearby [[Secunderabad]] followed in 1925.{{citation needed|date=November 2016}} In 1923, it acquired the '''Tata Industrial Bank''' in the wake of the failure of the [[Alliance Bank of Simla]]. The Tata Bank, established in 1917, had opened a branch in Madras in 1920 that became the Central Bank of India, Madras.{{citation needed|date=November 2016}} The Central Bank of India was instrumental in the creation of the first Indian exchange bank, the Central Exchange Bank of India, which opened in [[London]] in 1936. However, [[Barclays]] Bank acquired Central Exchange Bank of India in 1938.Raychaudhuri, Tappan, Irfan Habib, & Dharma Kumar, eds. (1983) ''The Cambridge Economic History of India: Volume 2, c.1751-c.1970''. (CUP Archive). p. 782. {{ISBN|9780521228022}} Also, before World War II, the Central Bank of India established a branch in [[Rangoon]]. The branch's operations concentrated on business between [[Burma]] and India, especially money transfers conducted via telegraph. Profits were derived primarily from the margins on [[Foreign exchange market|foreign exchange]]. The bank also provided loans accepting assets such as land, produce or other goods as collateral. Most of the banks customers were Indian businesses.Turnell, pp. 116–7. ===Post-World War II=== In 1963, the [[Politics of Burma#Military socialist era|revolutionary government]] in Burma nationalized the Central Bank of India's operations there, which became People's Bank No. 1.Turnell, p. 226. In 1969, the [[Government of India|Indian Government]] [[Indian banking#Nationalisation|nationalized]] the bank on 19 July, together with 13 others. [[File:Nameboard_of_Central_Bank_of_India_.jpg|thumb|Nameboard of Central Bank of India, Shankar Sheth Road Branch, Pune.]] [[File:Central Bank of India building at Brabourne Road in Kolkata.jpg|thumb|Central Bank of India, Brabourne Road Branch (in blue), in Kolkata.]] Central Bank of India was one of the first banks in India to issue credit cards in the year 1980 in collaboration with [[Visa Inc.|Visa]].{{Cite web |date=2020-07-20 |title=The Evolution of Cards: From Charge Plates to Contactless Cards - Razorpay Business |url=https://razorpay.com/blog/history-credit-debit-cards-visa-mastercard/ |access-date=2025-04-12 |language=en-US}} On its 108th Foundation Day, the Central Bank of India launched its first step towards robotic banking, a robot named "MEDHA". CBI is one of twelve public sector banks in India that was [[Recapitalization|recapitalised]] in 2009.{{cite news |date=18 February 2009 |title=18 govt banks to be recapitalised |newspaper=Business Standard India |publisher=Business-standard.com |url=http://business-standard.com/india/storypage.php?autono=349393 |access-date=2 August 2010}} As of 31 March 2021, the bank has a network of 4,608 branches, 3,644 [[Automated_teller_machine|ATM]]s, ten satellite offices, and one extension counter. It has a pan-India presence covering all 28 states, seven out of eight union territories, and 574 district headquarters out of all districts in the country. [[Reserve_Bank_of_India|RBI]]'s [[Federal_Deposit_Insurance_Corporation_Improvement_Act_of_1991#Prompt_Corrective_Action|prompt corrective action]] (PCA) came out last in the public sector in 2022. The PCA framework blocked large loans, restricted dividend payments, and restricted expenses.{{Cite news|lang=en|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/central-bank-of-india-last-to-exit-pca/articleshow/94338928.cms|title=Central Bank of India last to exit PCA|website=The Times of India|date=21 September 2022 |access-date=2024-03-25|archive-date=2022-09-25|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220925175946/https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/central-bank-of-india-last-to-exit-pca/articleshow/94338928.cms}} In 2024, Central Bank of India [[Governor]] MV Rao became chairman of the [[Indian_Banks%27_Association|Indian Banks Association]].{{Cite web|lang=en|url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/money-and-banking/central-bank-of-india-chief-executive-m-v-rao-elected-as-indian-banks-association-chairman/article67975707.ece|title=Central Bank of India chief executive M V Rao elected as Indian Banks' Association Chairman|website=The Hindu Businessline|date=21 March 2024 |access-date=2024-03-25|archive-date=2024-03-21|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240321120743/https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/money-and-banking/central-bank-of-india-chief-executive-m-v-rao-elected-as-indian-banks-association-chairman/article67975707.ece}} ==Subsidiaries== * Centbank Financial Services Limited, wholly owned subsidiary of Central Bank of India * Cent Bank Home Finance. As on 31st March, 2025, the CBI holds 64% stake. == Controversies == In the 1980s, the managers of the London branches of Central Bank of India, [[Punjab National Bank]], and [[Union Bank of India]] were caught up in a fraud in which they made dubious loans to the Bangladeshi jute trader Rajender Singh Sethia.{{Cite web |title=Businessman Rajender Singh Sethia fought 34-year-long legal battle to prove innocence |url=https://www.newindianexpress.com/nation/2019/jul/16/businessman-rajender-singh-sethia-fought-34-year-long-legal-battle-to-prove-innocence-2004350.html |access-date=2022-04-23 |website=The New Indian Express|date=15 July 2019 }} The regulatory authorities in England and India forced all three Indian banks to close their London branches. ==References== {{Reflist|30em}} ==Cited sources== {{commons category}} *Turnell, Sean (2009) ''Fiery Dragons: Banks, Moneylenders and Microfinance in Burma''. extract: The Central Bank of India (CBI) is an Indian public sector bank with its head office in Mumbai. Despite its name, CBI is not the central bank of India, a role served by the Reserve Bank of India.
